result.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification
result.summary: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. Built on Icarus Verilog and a CodeV-derived corpus, CSCA is evaluated on VerilogEval~2.0 and RTLLM~v2.0, including both code completion and specification-to-RTL tasks. With a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct backbone, CSCA leads the evaluated 7B-scale models and remains comparable to the much larger GPT-5.4-mini on the reported Verilog-generation benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对 Verilog 代码生成中仿真只给出模块级通过/失败的粗粒度反馈问题，提出 CSCA：先在信号级做连续行为验证，再对输出驱动的赋值语句片段施加五种反事实干预，将信号误差变化与行为一致性合成为语句级 credit，并映射为 token 权重用于加权 DPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其反事实干预＋连续 credit 映射为 token 权重的方法线索，可能可供核查如何为 latent 推理轨迹提供步骤级贡献分配与训练监督，但任务与视觉/多模态推理相距较远，迁移可行性需自行判断。
